newsitem.title: DUBAI: Ekeus said to be planning Gulf Arab tour.
newsitem.headline: Ekeus said to be planning Gulf Arab tour.

text.p: The U.N. official in charge of destroying Iraq's deadliest weapons was on Wednesday quoted as saying he planned to tour Gulf Arab states this month to seek funds and inform them of the results of his work in Iraq.

Al-Ittihad newspaper of the United Arab Emirates said in a Washington-datelined story that Rolf Ekeus, the Swedish diplomat who heads the special U.N. arms-disposal commission, said he planned to start his tour in Kuwait on November 22.
It said he will also visit the other Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman and the UAE "to inform their leaders on the results of his commission's work in Iraq".

"He said he hoped to receive financial aid from Kuwait and the GCC countries and from the United States, Germany, Japan and France to support the continued work of the commission, otherwise its work might have to stop."
Ekeus said he needed $36 million to support for one year the work of the U.N. Special Commission on Iraq, which runs inspections by about 100 U.N. personnel based in Baghdad, the paper added.
Iraq is required to declare banned weapons and other material it had promised to destroy after being defeated in the 1991 Gulf War sparked by Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The commission had been scheduled to collect much of the $36 million in annual operating expenses from the plan to let Iraq sell up to $2 billion in oil for relief supplies over a six-month period.
The plan was held up after Iraqi troops pushed into Kurdish territory in August, setting off U.S. missile attacks.

Ekeus said on Tuesday he would try a new tack with Iraqi political leaders next month in an effort to win their cooperation and would confront Deputy Prime Minister Tariq Aziz with what U.N. inspectors know about missing Iraqi ballistic missiles rather than wait for an Iraqi accounting.
